learning_objective: 🎯 Witness the transformation of a frightened, stuttering girl into a confident woman! Understand the power of education and a teacher's encouragement.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Bholi (real name Sulekha) fell off a cot as a baby, damaging her brain slightly. She also had pockmarks from smallpox and stammered. Her family ignored her and treated her like a 'dumb cow'.
Because of a government order, her father (Ramlal) sends her to school. Bholi is terrified, but her teacher is incredibly kind, soft-spoken, and encourages her to speak without fear.
Years pass. Her parents arrange her marriage to Bishamber, a rich but much older, limping grocer. Bishamber sees Bholi's pockmarks during the wedding and demands 5,000 rupees as dowry to marry her.
Ramlal puts his turban at Bishamber's feet and gives the money. But Bholi throws the garland into the fire. Without stammering, she refuses to marry a greedy, heartless man.
Bholi decides to stay single, teach in her old school, and take care of her old parents. Her teacher watches this, feeling the deep satisfaction of an artist viewing her 'masterpiece'.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 Paint Your Masterpiece
fun_activity.instructions: The teacher felt Bholi was her masterpiece. If you could teach someone one skill to make them confident (like speaking, drawing, coding), what would it be and why?

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast Bholi's treatment at home (neglected, old clothes) with her treatment at school (affection, clean clothes, books).
📌 Character sketch of the Teacher: Kind, empathetic, patient, and the true catalyst for Bholi's transformation.
📌 Explain why Bholi's real name 'Sulekha' is significant (it means 'one with good handwriting/destiny', which she proves true at the end).
quick_recap: ⭐ The story is a powerful critique of the dowry system and discrimination based on looks.
⭐ Education gave Bholi a voice, quite literally stopping her stammer.
⭐ Bholi's final decision shows true women empowerment and self-respect.
